body.statement: For every finite connected \(G\), integer \(2\le K\le R\), symmetric rational matrix \(\Sigma\), and positive integer \(N_{\exp}\), projecting any feasible point of \(\mathrm{MILP}(G,K,\Sigma,N_{\exp})\) to its \(x\)-label assignment yields a labeled partition \(\mathcal C=(C_1,\ldots,C_K)\in\mathfrak C_K(G)\). Every labeled \(\mathcal C\in\mathfrak C_K(G)\) has at least one feasible extension to the auxiliary variables, and every such extension has objective exactly \(V(\mathcal C;\Sigma)\). Auxiliary root and flow variables may admit multiple feasible extensions of the same labeled partition; this multiplicity is harmless, and cluster labels are not quotiented by permutations. Consequently the MILP optimum equals \(\min_{\mathcal C\in\mathfrak C_K(G)}V(\mathcal C;\Sigma)\), and projecting any MILP optimizer reconstructs an optimal labeled partition \(\mathcal C^\star\).
body.justification: Projection and feasible auxiliary extension establish a solver-ready exact formulation for arbitrary finite instances without requiring auxiliary-variable uniqueness, and provide a benchmark for the parameterized algorithm.
body.gap: Section 3.2 of Zhu et al. explains and justifies omitting its second-order residual-covariance term from graph-cut optimization; no published formulation located globally optimizes the resulting exact rational scope objective over connected nonempty clusters.
body.consumer: Experimenters with moderate graphs can obtain an auditable exact spatial cluster design rather than a heuristic candidate.
